title: add install script
description:
Closes https://github.com/posit-dev/jupyter-positron-server/issues/27
Closes https://github.com/posit-dev/jupyter-positron-server/issues/28

## Summary

Adds ready-made ways to deploy Positron Server on JupyterHub so admins don't
have to follow the manual Get Started steps by hand. Two supported paths:

- **TLJH** — a one-shot install script (`scripts/install-positron.sh`)
- **Single-host docker-compose** — a `docker/` deployment template

Plus documentation for both, and experimental (untested) Kubernetes notes kept
in-repo but out of the docs site.

## What's included

### `scripts/install-positron.sh` — TLJH one-shot installer
Runs once as root on a TLJH host and performs every Get Started step: downloads
& unpacks Positron Server, installs the license and signing key, installs
`jupyter-positron-server` (user env) and `jupyter-positron-verifier` (hub env),
generates the JupyterHub config that registers the verifier service, and reloads
TLJH. Fully configurable via environment variables (`--help` lists them);
self-contained so it can be distributed on its own.

### `docker/` — docker-compose deployment template
- `hub/` — JupyterHub + DockerSpawner image that runs the verifier and holds the
  secrets
- `singleuser/` — Positron session image (holds no secrets; fetches a minted
  token at session start)
- `docker-compose.yml`, `.env.example`, and a `README.md` with the token-flow
  diagram and configuration reference
- Secrets are bind-mounted read-only, never baked into images; the hub **fails
  fast at boot** if a secret is missing.

### Docs
- New **Deployment templates** page (`docs/deployment.qmd`) covering both paths,
  wired into the navbar
- Cross-link from **Get Started**, reframed as the manual walkthrough

title: docs: split out legacy instructions, simplify workflow
description:
Positron 2026.07.0+ replaces the old license-file setup with a signing-key/minting flow, so the existing get-started docs no longer matched what admins need to do.

- Rewrote docs/get_started.qmd for the new workflow (signing key + license minting via jupyter-positron-verifier, TLJH-specific pip paths, moved architecture diagram after the walkthrough)
- Added docs/legacy_get_started.qmd preserving the old (2026.05.0 and earlier) setup instructions for admins still on older releases, with a callout linking each guide to the other
- Simplified README.md and docs/index.qmd to point at the Get Started guide instead of duplicating install steps
- Bumped the required Positron Server version in docs/configuration.qmd to >= 2026.07.0-365

title: update server call to use `jupyter-positron-verifier`
description:
part of https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-builds/issues/984

## Add Hub license minting support

Introduces a `POSITRON_LICENSE_MINTING_ENDPOINT` environment variable that enables JupyterHub deployments to issue short-lived, per-session signed license tokens instead of relying on a static license file on disk.

### What changed

**`__init__.py`**

- Added `_fetch_license_from_hub(minting_endpoint, connection_token)` — makes an authenticated POST to the Hub minting service using `JUPYTERHUB_API_TOKEN` and returns the signed license JSON, or `None` on failure.
- When `POSITRON_LICENSE_MINTING_ENDPOINT` is set, `proxy_config_dict["command"]` is set to a **callable** instead of a static list. `jupyter-server-proxy` calls the function at each session start, so a fresh token is fetched at launch time rather than at import time.
- Braces in the license JSON are escaped (`{` → `{{`, `}` → `}}`) to prevent `jupyter-server-proxy`'s `format_map()` from interpreting them as template variables.
- `POSITRON_LICENSE_MINTING_ENDPOINT` takes precedence over `POSITRON_LICENSE_KEY_FILE`; the legacy static-file path is unchanged when the minting endpoint is not set.

**Tests**

- `TestHubMintedLicense`: verifies that `command` is callable when the minting endpoint is set, that `POSITRON_LICENSE_KEY=` is injected on success and absent on failure, that `--license-key-file` is never passed on the minting path, and that `--connection-token` is always present.
- `TestFetchLicenseFromHub`: covers missing `JUPYTERHUB_API_TOKEN`, successful response, network errors, and responses missing the `license` field.

**Docs**

- Rewrote `get_started.qmd` as a step-by-step Hub administrator guide for the new minting architecture (install binary, install `jupyter-positron-server` in the user image, install `jupyter-positron-verifier` on the Hub, register the service, configure the spawner).
- Added `POSITRON_LICENSE_MINTING_ENDPOINT` to the configuration table in `configuration.qmd` with a new "Hub License Minting" section.

### Architecture

```
Hub (privileged)
  signing-key.pem + license.lic  ← never reaches users
  jupyter-positron-verifier       ← mints a token per session

Single-user server
  jupyter-positron-server         ← fetches token at launch, passes via env
  positron-server                 ← verifies RSA signature, starts
```

title: pass in a reasonable default folder
description:
Closes #5

This PR passes `--default-folder` to `positron-server` so users land in a meaningful directory automatically, vs no workspace.

The folder is resolved with this priority:

  1. `JSP_DEFAULT_FOLDER` — explicit override for admins or users who need full control
  2. `JUPYTERHUB_ROOT_DIR` — the standard JupyterHub env var set when Spawner.notebook_dir is configured; covers most production deployments with no extra configuration
  3. `HOME` — always-available fallback that works in any single-user context

 The issue asks to open Positron in the same folder the user is actively browsing in JupyterLab. That would require knowing which subfolder is open in JupyterLab's file browser — but that state lives in the browser's localStorage on the client side, not in any server-side env var that positron-server can read at launch time.
  
Bridging that gap would require a JupyterLab extension that captures the current path and either writes it to a file or encodes it in the redirect URL before handing off to Positron. This PR addresses the 80% case: getting users into the right root directory instead of the filesystem root.

title: update path handling for custom urls
description:
Addresses 3 issues since they're small, related changes: #20 #19 #18 

Fixes path handling for JupyterHub deployments that use a custom `base_url`.

## Changes

- **`_make_mappath` and `rewrite_response`**: regex patterns now read `JUPYTERHUB_BASE_URL` from the environment and include it as a prefix, so path matching works correctly when JupyterHub is deployed under a sub-path (e.g. `/jh/`). The capture group is also made optional to handle paths that end exactly at `/positron` with no trailing segment.
- **`which_positron_server`**: returns the full resolved path from `which()` rather than the bare program name string.
- **`setup_positron_server`**: adds `--server-base-path` to the Positron Server launch arguments, derived from `JUPYTERHUB_SERVICE_PREFIX`. This argument is required for Positron Server to serve HTTP responses correctly when running under a sub-path.

title: rewrite response for doubled paths
description:
When running positron-server behind jupyter-server-proxy (e.g., on TLJH), the connection token validation redirect doubles the URL path, eg, http://localhost:8080/user/admin/positron/user/admin/positron instead of http://localhost:8080/user/admin/positron.

  - Add rewrite_response function to fix redirect Location headers                                                  
  - Clear X-Forwarded-Prefix header to prevent positron-server from constructing doubled URLs
  - Add trailing slash to launcher path for proper redirects
